title: How to check if an image is AI-generated #Shorts
description:
There's no single perfect test for AI images, but four checks catch a lot. Narrated with an AI voice.

#AI #Deepfake #FactCheck #Shorts

segments.say: That viral image. Is it real, or made by AI? There's no single perfect test, but four checks catch a lot.
One. Zoom in. Look at hands, text, jewellery, reflections and backgrounds. AI still slips on small details, though it's getting better.
Two. Do a reverse image search. See where it first appeared, and whether trusted news outlets are using it.
Three. Some tools now attach content credentials, a label in the file saying how it was made. If a site shows them, read them. Missing credentials don't prove anything either way.
Four. Ask who posted it first, and why. Emotional, shocking images are the ones to slow down on.
When in doubt, don't share. Follow for more AI safety tips.

title: Why AI text detectors can't be trusted #Shorts
description:
AI writing detectors make mistakes, including flagging human writing as AI. Why, and what to do instead. Narrated with an AI voice.

#AI #Education #AIdetector #Shorts

segments.say: Can a tool reliably tell whether text was written by AI? Not reliably, no.
AI detectors look for patterns, like how predictable the wording is. But plain, careful human writing can look predictable too.
So detectors can flag real human work as AI. Writers using a second language and very formal writers can be flagged unfairly. And lightly edited AI text can slip through.
A detector score shouldn't be the only evidence against anyone. Look at drafts, version history, or just talk to the person about their work.
Evidence, not scores. Follow for more AI explained.

title: Is your AI chat being used for training? Check this #Shorts
description:
Two privacy settings to check in any AI chatbot before you share personal details. Narrated with an AI voice.

#AI #Privacy #ChatGPT #Shorts

segments.say: Before you tell an AI chatbot something personal, check two settings.
One. Does the company use your conversations to improve its models? Many apps let you switch this off in settings, but the default varies by app and by plan.
Two. How long are chats kept, and can you delete them? Look for chat history or data controls.
Business and education plans often have different rules from free personal accounts. If you use AI at work, ask what your employer has agreed to.
If you can't find a clear answer, leave out names, addresses, health details and passwords. Follow for more AI safety tips.

title: Why does AI need GPUs? #Shorts
description:
AI runs on graphics chips because they can do huge amounts of simple maths at the same time. Narrated with an AI voice.

#AI #GPU #AIexplained #Shorts

segments.say: Why are graphics chips, made for video games, now powering AI?
Under the hood, an AI model is mostly multiplying and adding enormous grids of numbers.

segments.screen: CPU: a few at a time
segments.say: A normal processor is great at doing a few complicated things quickly, one after another.
A graphics chip has thousands of simpler cores that work at the same time. That's ideal for drawing pixels, and also for the maths inside AI.
Memory matters just as much, because the whole model has to fit somewhere fast. That's why AI chips are in such demand. Follow for more AI explained.

title: Does AI learn from your chats? Training vs using #Shorts
description:
Training builds an AI model. Inference is using it. Why a chatbot doesn't instantly learn from your conversation. Narrated with an AI voice.

#AI #MachineLearning #AIexplained #Shorts

segments.say: When you correct a chatbot, does it learn and remember for everyone? Usually not instantly.
Training is when a model is built. It studies huge amounts of data over weeks or months, and its internal numbers are adjusted.
Inference is when you use the finished model. Your chat runs through it, but the model's numbers don't change while you talk.
When an app remembers you, that's usually a separate memory feature storing notes, not the model retraining. And your chats might be used in future training, depending on your settings.
So check your privacy settings. Follow for more AI explained.

title: The 4-part prompt that fixes bad AI answers #Shorts
description:
Most weak AI answers come from vague prompts. A simple four-part structure that works in any chatbot. Narrated with an AI voice.

#AI #PromptEngineering #ChatGPT #Shorts

segments.say: Getting bland answers from AI? Add these four parts to your prompt.
One. The task, stated clearly. Not just write an email, but write a reply declining this meeting politely.
Two. The context. Who it's for, what they already know, and anything the AI can't guess.
Three. An example of what good looks like. Paste something you've written before, so it copies your style.
Four. The format. Length, bullet points or paragraphs, and the tone.
Task, context, example, format. Try it on your next prompt. Follow for more AI tips.

title: Why AI struggles to count letters in a word #Shorts
description:
Ask some chatbots how many letters are in a word and they can slip up. The reason is tokens. Narrated with an AI voice.

#AI #LLM #AIexplained #Shorts

segments.say: AI can write an essay in seconds, but some models have tripped up counting the letters in a word. Why?
Language models don't read letter by letter. They read tokens, which are chunks of text. A whole word might be one or two tokens.
So the individual letters inside a chunk aren't directly in front of the model. It has to infer them, and that's where slips happen.
Newer models often handle this better, especially when they reason step by step or use a tool like code.
For exact counting and maths, ask the AI to use a calculator or code, or check it yourself. Follow for more AI explained.

title: AI vs machine learning vs deep learning #Shorts
description:
Three terms people mix up, explained with one picture: circles inside circles. Narrated with an AI voice.

#AI #MachineLearning #DeepLearning #Shorts

segments.screen: AI vs ML vs deep learning
segments.say: AI, machine learning, deep learning. What's the difference? Picture circles inside circles.
Artificial intelligence is the big circle. Any technique that gets computers to do tasks we'd call intelligent.
Inside it is machine learning. Instead of writing every rule by hand, the system learns patterns from examples.
Inside that is deep learning. Machine learning using large neural networks with many layers. It powers today's chatbots, image generators and voice tools.
All deep learning is machine learning, and all machine learning is AI. Not the other way round. Follow for more AI explained.

title: How AI understands meaning: embeddings explained #Shorts
description:
Embeddings turn words into lists of numbers so that similar meanings land close together. That's how AI search finds what you mean. Narrated with an AI voice.

#AI #Embeddings #AIexplained #Shorts

segments.say: How does AI search know that cheap flights and budget airfare mean the same thing?
With embeddings. A model turns a piece of text into a long list of numbers that captures its meaning.
Texts with similar meanings get similar numbers, so they land close together, like points on a map.
To search, your question is turned into numbers too, and the system finds the closest matches, even if they share no words.
It's how AI tools search your documents and recommend similar things. Follow for more AI explained.

title: What is multimodal AI? #Shorts
description:
Multimodal AI can work with text, images, audio and more in one model. What it's good for, and its limits. Narrated with an AI voice.

#AI #MultimodalAI #AIexplained #Shorts

segments.say: You've heard AI can now see, hear and talk. That's called multimodal AI.
Multimodal means one model can handle more than one kind of input or output. Text, images, audio, and sometimes video.
Snap a photo of a broken part and ask what it is. Upload a chart and ask for the key point. Talk to it out loud.
The same limits still apply. It can misread an image just as confidently as it misstates a fact.
So double check anything important. Follow for more AI explained.

title: Use AI to actually learn, not just get answers #Shorts
description:
Three ways to use AI as a study partner that makes you better, not lazier. Check your school's AI rules. Narrated with an AI voice.

#AI #Study #StudyTips #Shorts

segments.say: Using AI to do your homework teaches you nothing. Using it like a tutor can teach you a lot.
One. Ask it to explain a topic simply, then explain it back in your own words, and ask it what you got wrong.
Two. Paste your notes and say, quiz me one question at a time, and don't give me the answer until I try.
Three. Check anything you'll be graded on against your textbook or teacher. AI can be confidently wrong.
And check your school's rules on AI before you use it for assessed work. Follow for more practical AI.

title: Is the AI on your phone sending your data to the cloud? #Shorts
description:
Some AI features run on your device, others in the cloud. Why it matters for privacy and how to check. Narrated with an AI voice.

#AI #Privacy #Smartphone #Shorts

segments.say: When your phone uses AI, is it thinking on the phone, or sending your data somewhere else?
Some features run on the device itself. Your data stays on the phone, and it can even work offline. But the models are smaller.
Other features send your request to a company's servers, where bigger models do the work. More powerful, but your data leaves the phone.
Many phones now mix both, choosing based on the task. The privacy details vary by brand and feature.
Look in your phone's AI or privacy settings for what's processed where. Follow for more AI explained.
